blind.description: A medieval or fantasy half-timber wall section featuring a central rectangular doorway opening. It consists of heavy dark brown wooden corner posts, a top header beam, a horizontal transom beam defining the door height, and inner vertical jambs. Cream-colored plaster or daub panels fill the spaces above the door and in thin vertical bands flanking each side of the opening. All surfaces are clean, solid, and textured with painted wood grain and stucco shading.
blind.from_above: A narrow horizontal dark brown rectangle with slightly wider, chamfered caps at each end representing the top of the timber posts.
blind.height_vs_figure: Overall height is roughly 6.5 to 7 feet (slightly taller than the 5 ft 9 in figure), with a width of approximately 5 feet; the door opening itself is around 4.5 to 5 feet high.
